description: Figure 5(b) is a line plot illustrating the ratio of training loss values for different methods relative to the Vanilla baseline, plotted against the cumulative FLOPs (floating-point operations) incurred during training. The x-axis, labeled "FLOPs," is on a linear scale ranging from 0 to approximately 140,000, with tick marks at intervals of 20,000. The y-axis, labeled "Loss Ratio," is also on a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 1.0, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The plot contains five distinct lines, each representing a different method: Vanilla (purple, solid line), StrmLLM (n=64) (blue, solid line), SepLLM (n=64) (orange, solid line), SepLLM (n=64, H) (green, solid line), and SepLLM (n=64, H/T) (red, solid line). All lines start at a loss ratio of 1.0 at the beginning of training (0 FLOPs) and decrease as FLOPs increase, indicating that the loss for all methods improves relative to Vanilla. The StrmLLM (n=64) line (blue) shows the steepest initial decline, reaching a loss ratio of approximately 0.85 by 20,000 FLOPs and continuing to decrease to about 0.75 by 140,000 FLOPs. The SepLLM (n=64) line (orange) follows a similar but slightly less steep trajectory, ending at a loss ratio of approximately 0.80. The SepLLM (n=64, H) line (green) and SepLLM (n=64, H/T) line (red) show more gradual declines, with the latter ending at a loss ratio of approximately 0.85. The Vanilla line (purple) remains constant at a loss ratio of 1.0 throughout the entire range of FLOPs, serving as the baseline for comparison.
